citations.quote: The client says: We’re not interested anymore.

cue.text: Clients say they are not interested anymore.

citations.quote: You won the argument. And lost the client.

outcome.text: The agent wins the argument but loses the client.

citations.quote: Then you shouldn’t have clicked on the advertisement. Ads cost money and you just wasted it.

response.text: The agent says clients shouldn't have clicked on the advertisement if they weren't interested, implicitly blaming them for wasting money.

citations.quote: One of the agents in a recent coaching session told me this is exactly what he says to clients...Ads cost money and you just wasted it.

situation.text: An agent reacts to clients who say they are not interested by blaming them for wasting advertising money.

cases.title: Agent Blaming Clients for Ad Costs

citations.quote: Please follow carefully. 😇 Bad advice #1: Before you WhatsApp the lead, send an email first. Especially if they are European or American.

observation.text: The text uses sarcasm and humor to critique conventional sales advice by labeling them as 'Bad advice.'

expression.title: Humor and Irony in Sales Tips

citations.quote: Bad advice #1: Before you WhatsApp the lead,
Bad advice #2: If you call, speak REALLY fast.
Bad advice #3: Keep looking for the perfect script for every client.
Bad advice #4: If they say they are not interested, tell them they just wasted your advertising money.

observation.text: The author lists incorrect sales advice sequentially, using numbers to differentiate each piece of bad advice.

citations.quote: And no, I am not exaggerating.
And if any of these “sales tips” felt slightly too familiar 😂, share this post with someone who might urgently need them.

observation.text: The text employs sarcasm by praising poor sales tactics to emphasize their ineffectiveness, and then transitions with a corrective perspective.

citations.quote: They do not answer immediately? - Not serious. They ask for a cheaper option? - Not serious. They say they are “just exploring”? - Definitely not serious. 😅

summary.text: Clients who do not answer immediately, ask for cheaper options, or say they are "just exploring" may be identified as "not serious" by sales agents.

citations.quote: Ideally, give them enough time to completely forget they ever clicked on the advertisement.

summary.text: Being too formal, like sending emails before making contact through WhatsApp, might cause potential clients to forget about their initial inquiry.

citations.quote: The problem is that you still do not know how to lead the conversation when the client says something unexpected.

summary.text: Searching for market-specific scripts may not resolve client interaction issues; the real problem may be in handling unexpected client responses.

knowledge.title: Ineffectiveness of Scripts for Different Markets

citations.quote: One of the agents in a recent coaching session told me this is exactly what he says to clients...Ads cost money and you just wasted it.

summary.text: Some agents have reportedly told clients that they wasted advertising money by not being interested after clicking on an ad, which can lead to losing the client.

knowledge.title: Interaction Mistake: Blaming Clients for Advertising Costs

citations.quote: The goal is not to memorise every possible answer. It is to understand how to lead the conversation.

summary.text: The goal in client interactions should not be to memorize answers but to understand how to lead conversations effectively.
